panels.title: Every kind, over time
panels.description: Stacks the count of every Event over time, one series per kind, including a record that reached no kind. A label_format step renames an empty kind to the literal "none" before grouping, because an empty kind interpolates to an empty legend name, and Grafana then falls back to the raw field name "Value" instead of a readable series name, so the shape of a session is visible with every series legible.

targets.expr: sum by (kind) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | label_format kind=`{{ if .kind }}{{ .kind }}{{ else }}none{{ end }}` [$__interval]))

panels.title: Model calls per minute
panels.description: Counts kind=model_call Events in fixed one-minute buckets, over time.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" [1m]))

panels.title: Tool calls per minute, by tool
panels.description: Stacks kind=tool_call Events in fixed one-minute buckets, one series per tool attribute.

targets.expr: sum by (tool) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" [1m]))

panels.title: Calls per tool, top 20
panels.description: Shows the top 20 tools by call count over the selected range, counting kind=tool_call Events grouped by the tool attribute, as a horizontal bar chart.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (tool) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" [$__range])))

panels.title: Tool calls by tool_type, mcp against native
panels.description: Reads tool_type on kind=tool_call Events over the selected range, split between mcp and native. A reduceOptions block (every other single-value panel in this module already carries one) tells the piechart how to collapse each tool_type series to one slice value. reduceOptions.values is true, not false: an instant Loki query returns one table-shaped frame with tool_type as a string column and Value as the numeric column, one row per series, so the panel needs one slice per ROW, not one slice for the whole numeric column. With values: false the piechart drew a single whole slice named "Value #A" instead of one slice per tool_type.

targets.expr: sum by (tool_type) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" [$__range]))

panels.title: Tool call success rate
panels.description: Divides the kind=tool_call Events whose success attribute is true by all kind=tool_call Events over the selected range, as a percentage.

targets.expr: 100 * sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" | success="true" [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" [$__range]))

panels.title: Failed tool calls, over time
panels.description: Counts kind=tool_call Events whose success attribute is false, over time, one series per tool.

targets.expr: sum by (tool) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" | success="false" [$__interval]))

panels.title: MCP server errors, by error type
panels.description: Reads mcp_server.error.type on kind=mcp_server_call Events whose status attribute is error, counted over the selected range, one bar per error type.

targets.expr: sum by (mcp_server_error_type) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="mcp_server_call" | mcp_server_status="error" [$__range]))

panels.title: MCP server cache hit ratio
panels.description: Divides the kind=mcp_server_call Events whose mcp_server.cache attribute is hit by all kind=mcp_server_call Events that report a cache state, over the selected range, as a percentage. Only 184 mcp_server_call records exist, so this gauge can read thin.

targets.expr: 100 * sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="mcp_server_call" | mcp_server_cache="hit" [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="mcp_server_call" | mcp_server_cache!="" [$__range]))

panels.title: Active sessions, over time
panels.description: Counts the distinct session_id values emitting any Event in each time bucket, over time.

targets.expr: count(count by (session_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} [$__interval])))

panels.title: Session activity, by session
panels.description: Shows one row per session_id, limited to the top 20 sessions by Event count over the selected range, counting every Event over time, so a gap in a row shows when that session was not emitting. Each row is labelled by the first 8 characters of session_id, because the full 36-character identifier overlaps and becomes unreadable as a row label. The panel is 24 grid rows tall, rather than the 8 rows every other panel on this board uses, because twenty state-timeline rows need the extra height to stay legible.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (session_short) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | label_format session_short=`{{ substr 0 8 .session_id }}` [$__interval])))

panels.title: Model calls per session, top 20
panels.description: Shows the top 20 session_id values by model call count over the selected range, counting kind=model_call Events, as a horizontal bar chart. Each bar is labelled by the first 8 characters of session_id, because the full 36-character identifier overlaps and becomes unreadable on the category axis.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (session_short) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | label_format session_short=`{{ substr 0 8 .session_id }}` [$__range])))

panels.title: Run pass rate
panels.description: Divides the kind=run_end Events whose pass attribute is true by all kind=run_end Events over the selected range, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1 under the percentunit unit, so Grafana renders it as a percentage. The query no longer multiplies by 100 itself: that extra multiplication produced a figure like 1.4 under the unrelated unit=short, which reads as neither a 0-to-1 proportion nor a clearly labelled percentage. The `or (... * 0)` term reports a true zero when no Event in range has pass="true", and no Event is fabricated. Only 304 run_end records exist, so this stat can read thin.

targets.expr: (sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" | pass="true" [$__range])) or (sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" [$__range])) * 0)) / sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" [$__range]))

panels.title: Wall time per run
panels.description: Reads wall_ms on kind=run_end Events over the selected range, the top 20 runs by wall time, one bar per run_id. Each bar is labelled by the first 8 characters of run_id with the replay- or conform- prefix stripped first, because the full identifier overlaps and becomes unreadable on the category axis, and because every replayed run_id shares the literal "replay-" prefix, which would collide if truncated without stripping it first. A direct Loki query against this exact expression (max by run_id of max_over_time wall_ms) confirms the arithmetic is a true per-run maximum, not a sum: the largest bar reflects one genuine recorded run_end Event at wall_ms=257529602 (about 71.5 hours), not a unit or aggregation bug. Only 304 run_end records exist, so this chart can read thin.

targets.expr: topk(20, max by (run_id_short) (max_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" | label_format run_id_short=`{{ trimPrefix "replay-" .run_id | trimPrefix "conform-" | substr 0 8 }}` | unwrap wall_ms [$__range])))

panels.title: Turns per run, over time
panels.description: Reads turns on kind=run_end Events, one series per run_id, over time. A run_end Event is a single point in time, so the lookback window is widened to a fixed 6 hours (rather than the panel-width-dependent $__interval) to hold each point visible across several consecutive steps, and points are drawn large and always-on rather than left to the default auto visibility, so an isolated run_end Event is still legible. Each series is labelled by the first 8 characters of run_id with the replay- or conform- prefix stripped first, because the full identifier overlaps and fills a third of the panel as a legend. Only 304 run_end records exist, so this chart can read thin.

targets.expr: max by (run_id_short) (max_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" | label_format run_id_short=`{{ trimPrefix "replay-" .run_id | trimPrefix "conform-" | substr 0 8 }}` | unwrap turns [6h]))

panels.title: Timed-out runs
panels.description: Counts kind=run_end Events whose timed_out attribute is true, over the selected range. The `or (... * 0)` term reports a true zero when no Event in range has timed_out="true", and no Event is fabricated. Only 304 run_end records exist, so this stat can read thin.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" | timed_out="true" [$__range])) or (sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="run_end" [$__range])) * 0)

panels.title: MCP server raw bytes against returned bytes, over time
panels.description: Sums mcp_server.raw_bytes and mcp_server.returned_bytes on kind=mcp_server_call Events, over time. Only 184 mcp_server_call records exist, so this chart can read thin.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="mcp_server_call" | mcp_server_raw_bytes != "" | unwrap mcp_server_raw_bytes [$__interval]))

sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="mcp_server_call" | mcp_server_returned_bytes != "" | unwrap mcp_server_returned_bytes [$__interval]))

panels.title: Result bytes per tool, top 20
panels.description: Sums result_bytes on kind=tool_call Events over the selected range, one named bar per tool, for the top 20 tools that report it. Rendered as a horizontal bar chart rather than a bar gauge: a bar gauge fed by this query drew a single unnamed bar whenever the result narrowed to one series, because a bar gauge with exactly one field hides its name label, while a bar chart always shows a labelled category per bar regardless of series count. result_bytes is present on a share of recorded kind=tool_call Events (the Claude Code Transcript parser sets it only when it can read tool_result_size_bytes), so a tool that never exposes it is absent from this panel rather than shown at zero.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (tool) (sum_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="tool_call" | result_bytes != "" | unwrap result_bytes [$__range])))
